title: Mid-Autumn Festival: Exploring Ancient Rituals at the Temple of the Moon, Expressing Good Wishes Beneath the Full Moon
description: BEIJING, Sept. 25, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- A news report from China.org.cn on the Mid-Autumn Festival: Mid-Autumn Festival: Exploring Ancient Rituals at the Temple of the Moon, Expressing Good Wishes Beneath the Full Moon The Mid-Autumn Festival marks an occasion to reunite with family and pray for blessings beneath the full moon for Chinese people. For thousands of years, the imperial rituals of moon worship blended with ordinary people's romantic reveries of the moon and stars, giving rise to unique folk customs and heartfelt warmth that define China's Mid-Autumn Festival. Autumn is the harvest season, and on the 15th day of the eighth lunar month, the moon is full and round. And for Chinese people, a full moon is a symbol of the whole family being together. Enjoying jasmine flowers, celebrating the harvest and having a big family dinner - all these reflect one simple wish: peace and togetherness. From the solemn imperial rituals of moon worship to lively and heartwarming folk customs, the Mid-Autumn Festival has kept evolving, yet people's longing for reunion and love for family has never faded. title: Komuravelli yields ancient mother goddess stone sculpture
description: KOMURAVELLI: An anthropomorphic stone believed to represent an ancient mother goddess has been identified near Mallanna Gutta in Komuravelli, Siddipet district, researcher Kolipaka Srinivas of the Kotha Telangana Charitra Brundam said. Stone carving may depict an early mother goddess Srinivas said a circular stone has a groove carved around its upper portion. The groove appears […] Stone carving may depict an early mother goddess Srinivas said a circular stone has a groove carved around its upper portion. The groove appears to have been designed to represent the head, with the lower portion depicting the body, he said. He identified it as an early mother goddess sculpture and said local tribal communities in ancient times may have worshipped such stones as protective mother deities. Similar stone found at megalithic burial site Srinivas said a one-foot-high rectangular stone pillar with similar groove markings was found by the archaeology department during excavations at the megalithic burial sites at Pullur. He said that artefact was the first representation of a mother goddess found in Telangana. The stone found at Komuravelli could belong to the Megalithic period, he said. Srinivas said such finds are rare and require further research to establish their historical significance. ]]>

title: Dravida — The Ancient Tamil Country of Rivers, Temples and the Southern Ocean
description: One of the clearest references appears in the Bhishma Parva during the epic's famous description of Bharatavarsha. When the southern regions are enumerated, the text names the Dravidas, Keralas, Mushikas and Vanavashikas, followed by Karanatakas, Mahishakas, Kuntalas, Cholas and many other peoples. The passage firmly places the Dravidas among the recognised countries and communities of southern Bharata.
